name: Saint John of the Cross
history: A Carmelite friar who worked with Saint Teresa of Ávila to reform his order and was imprisoned by his own brothers for it. In a tiny cell in Toledo he wrote his greatest poetry. The Dark Night and The Living Flame of Love map the way of the soul to union with God.
meditation: In the evening of life we shall be judged on love.
life: Juan de Yepes was born in 1542 at Fontiveros near Ávila. His father died young, and his mother brought up her sons in hard poverty. At Medina del Campo he worked in a hospital while studying with the Jesuits, and in 1563 he joined the Carmelites. Ordained in 1567, he was thinking of becoming a Carthusian when he met Teresa of Ávila, who persuaded him to help her reform. The next year at Duruelo he began the first house of the Discalced friars and took the name John of the Cross. In December 1577 friars opposed to the reform seized him and held him in their priory at Toledo, beaten and in darkness. There he composed much of the Spiritual Canticle. After nine months he escaped by night. In his last illness he was treated harshly by his own superior. He died at Úbeda in 1591 and was named a Doctor of the Church in 1926.
prayerTo: Saint John of the Cross, in a dark cell you found the living flame of God's love. Pray for all who walk through dryness, doubt or suffering, that they may trust that God is near. Teach me to let go of what holds me back from Him, and to seek Him above everything He gives. Amen.
penance: Give up one comfort today, offered freely for love of God. Spend ten minutes in silent prayer before a crucifix.
